evidence.claim: Nigeria has an IAEA comprehensive safeguards agreement in force and an Additional Protocol on the record, with nuclear physical protection and liability-related agreements also listed.
evidence.title: Country List : Office of Legal Affairs : IAEA
evidence.excerpt: Nigeria has an IAEA comprehensive safeguards agreement in force and an Additional Protocol on the record, with nuclear physical protection and liability-related agreements also listed.
evidence.source_locator: Safeguards Agreements table and Agreements table
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IAEA Office of Legal Affairs is the authoritative treaty-status source for member-state nuclear agreements.
evidence.period_fit: stable treaty and safeguards framework applicable in 2022
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional rather than personal, but directly relevant to what Buhari's government had to oversee in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The page is a status record, not proof of day-to-day compliance quality.
It does not show how much direct presidential attention the file received.

evidence.claim: Nigeria is described as a party to the NPT, CSA, Additional Protocol, Pelindaba Treaty, and CTBT, and the NNRA says it provides IAEA reporting and domestic inspections to keep material in peaceful use.
evidence.title: IAEA APPLAUDS SAFEGUARDS IMPLEMENTATION IN NIGERIA FOR THE FIRST TIME
evidence.excerpt: Nigeria is described as a party to the NPT, CSA, Additional Protocol, Pelindaba Treaty, and CTBT, and the NNRA says it provides IAEA reporting and domestic inspections to keep material in peaceful use.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary national regulator statement with explicit treaty and safeguards claims.
evidence.period_fit: framework active in 2022 and directly relevant to the 2022 safeguards environment
evidence.ruler_attribution: Governmental, not solely Buhari-personal, but part of the authority he headed in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The page references 2020 safeguards conclusions rather than a 2022 fresh audit.

evidence.claim: IAEA safeguards inspectors visited Nigeria on 27-28 June 2022 for physical inventory verification, and the page says the inspection was satisfactory and consistent with Nigeria's safeguards obligations.
evidence.title: NNRA HOSTED THE IAEA SAFEGUARDS INSPECTORS
evidence.excerpt: IAEA safeguards inspectors visited Nigeria on 27-28 June 2022 for physical inventory verification, and the page says the inspection was satisfactory and consistent with Nigeria's safeguards obligations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous regulator notice with exact dates and concrete inspection activity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Not personally Buhari-run, but it is the nuclear-security system his government was responsible for in 2022.
contrary_evidence: This is a regulator statement rather than an independent inspection report.
It covers safeguards compliance, not broader nuclear policy quality.

evidence.claim: In December 2022 Nigeria hosted an IAEA-backed SEED workshop to build capacity for site safety evaluation for a first nuclear power plant, with two sites selected and feasibility work underway.
evidence.title: NNRA and NAEC collaborate with IAEA to organize the National Workshop on SEED Capacity Building for Site Safety Evaluation and Review for New Nuclear Installation Programme in Nigeria.
evidence.excerpt: In December 2022 Nigeria hosted an IAEA-backed SEED workshop to build capacity for site safety evaluation for a first nuclear power plant, with two sites selected and feasibility work underway.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary national-regulator account with exact dates and explicit capacity-building purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects state policy and regulatory work under Buhari's administration, though not a personal crisis decision.
contrary_evidence: The source shows planning and training, not operational nuclear capability.
It does not show final investment or construction decisions.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Buhari decision on nuclear brinkmanship, command-and-control, or other existential-risk use of presidential authority.
No independent audit of whether the 2021-2022 safeguards and physical-protection framework was actually implemented in practice.
No direct evidence of Buhari personally directing external military operations, proxy conduct, or coercive cross-border action in 2022.
No substantive mediation track or concrete ceasefire result led by Buhari himself.
Independent, case-level follow-through on prosecutions and investigations for major 2022 abuses is thin.
Some severe insecurity items are still better understood as state failure in a violent environment than as direct ruler-directed violence.
No independent pre-election audit of how fully the Electoral Act 2022 was implemented before the 2023 polls.
Much of the affirmative evidence is self-description from Buhari and his administration.
Budget execution and capital-spending delivery are not independently audited at the project level here.
Household-level and regional distributional causality remains only partially evidenced.
Independent audit evidence on how much of the announced welfare and health delivery actually reached beneficiaries in 2022 is limited.
The chapter still mixes federal action, donor support, and inherited deprivation.
No direct 2022 evidence of Buhari's assets, procurement benefits, bribes, or formal audit/court findings tied to personal enrichment.
The family-appointment case is strong on patronage but still thin on Buhari's knowledge, benefit, and intent beyond approval.
The Lake Chad arms claim is shown as unsupported, but there is no public correction or retraction by Buhari in the package.
Independent audit-grade evidence on the delivery tracker and the administration's correction of weak implementers is still limited.
The chapter still depends heavily on macro outcomes that mix Buhari-era policy with inherited constraints and external shocks.
